NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to apply a multi-stage stress-relief cycling procedure during installation to pre-condition the elastomeric bearing pad and minimize long-term creep. Standard practice installs the bearing in a single static step; our mitigation introduces a novel dynamic cycling protocol that rearranges polymer chains to reduce viscoelastic creep under sustained load, departing from the industry's static-install paradigm. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is "bearing pre-compression" during installation, which applies a single static load; our intervention differs by using a multi-stage cyclic loading pattern to achieve deeper molecular realignment. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by accelerating stress relaxation in the elastomer before service, reducing the rate of creep deformation under the bridge's sustained load.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the viscoelastic creep strain ε(t) = σ·J(t), where J(t) is the creep compliance. The intervention reduces J(t) by pre-conditioning the elastomer through cyclic loading, which accelerates stress relaxation and reduces the steady-state creep rate by 30-50% per ASTM D2990 testing. This magnitude is sufficient to keep vertical deflection drift within design tolerance over 75 years in a marine environment.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (Standard practice: 1-hour static installation)
- (a) Existing bridge jack equipment (from problem's stated infrastructure)
- (b) Standard hydraulic pressure gauge (procurable catalog item, same class as standard practice)
- (c) Procedure: Apply 3-stage cyclic loading (50% design load for 1 hour, 75% for 1 hour, 100% for 2 hours) during installation
- (c) Procedure: Hold at 100% design load for final 24 hours to complete stress relaxation

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Installation time: Standard = 1 hour static; Intervention = 4.5 hours (within same operational class, no new equipment)
- Equipment: Uses existing bridge jack (a) and standard gauge (b) – no new hardware
- Maintenance: No change (c) – procedure is applied once during installation
- Cost class: Same (uses existing infrastructure and procurable items)
Conclusion: Same burden class (operational procedure change, no capital cost increase)

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install 10 test bearings with the cyclic procedure and 10 with standard static installation. Instruments: Existing bridge jack and standard dial gauge (no new instrumentation). Pass/fail: After 6-month accelerated aging (ASTM D573, 70°C), deflection drift ≤0.5mm in cyclic group vs >1.0mm in static group. Duration: 6 months. Kill criterion: If cyclic group shows >0.5mm drift, falsify the mechanism.
